name: GNSS/GPS Security Assessment
description: Ability to assess the security of Global Navigation Satellite System receivers and signals, including GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, and BeiDou. Covers GNSS signal structure analysis, spoofing attack generation and detection, meaconing assessment, receiver vulnerability testing, and evaluation of authentication mechanisms such as Galileo OSNMA and proposed GPS authentication mechanisms such as CHIMERA.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to GNSS security assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands GNSS signal architecture and known vulnerability classes
evidence: Can describe GPS/GNSS signal structure (L1 C/A, L2, L5) and positioning principles
Understands the difference between spoofing, meaconing, and jamming attacks
Completed training on GNSS security threats and assessment methodology

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Performs GNSS signal analysis and basic spoofing exercises in shielded environments under supervision
evidence: Captured and analyzed GNSS signals using SDR in a shielded environment under guidance
Generated simulated GPS signals using a GNSS simulator for receiver testing under supervision
Observed the effect of spoofed signals on GNSS receivers in controlled conditions

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses GNSS receiver security in controlled environments
evidence: Independently assessed GNSS receiver vulnerability to spoofing across 3+ receiver types
Conducted meaconing and signal replay attacks in shielded lab conditions
Evaluated receiver-level anti-spoofing mechanisms and detection capabilities
Produced reports documenting spoofing attack effectiveness, receiver behavior, and countermeasure recommendations

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Performs advanced GNSS spoofing scenarios; assesses navigation authentication mechanisms
evidence: Developed sophisticated spoofing scenarios including gradual position drift and time manipulation
Assessed Galileo OSNMA or GPS signal authentication implementations
Evaluated multi-constellation receiver resilience to targeted single-constellation attacks
Mentors junior analysts on GNSS assessment and develops custom spoofing profiles

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on GNSS security; publishes research; defines lab assessment methodology
evidence: Published research on GNSS spoofing, detection, or authentication mechanisms
Authored the lab's GNSS security assessment methodology
Discovered novel GNSS receiver vulnerabilities or spoofing techniques
Trains teams on GNSS security and advises on critical infrastructure GNSS hardening

assessment_methods.description: In a shielded lab environment, assess a GNSS receiver's vulnerability to spoofing attacks of increasing sophistication and document receiver behavior at each stage
Review GNSS security assessment reports for attack methodology rigor and countermeasure recommendation quality

equipment: Spirent GSS9000 or LabSat GNSS simulator
RF shielded enclosure for GNSS testing
